input.quote: The exclusive remedy of either party in a claim against the other under this Agreement shall be the recovery of its direct damages. In no event shall either party be liable to the other for the recovery of any special, indirect or consequential damages even if the defendant party had been advised of the possibility of such damages including but not limited to lost profits, lost revenues, failure to realize expected savings, loss of data and loss of use. ... The limitation of liability in this Section 15 shall not apply to breaches of Sections 13 and 14.
input.rationale: Section 15 is the only liability provision in the Agreement (no "aggregate liability" language appears anywhere else). It contains a mutual exclusion of indirect/consequential damages and carve-outs for Sections 13 (IP) and 14 (confidentiality), but no monetary cap of any kind, so each party's — including Sparkling's — exposure for direct damages is unlimited. That fails both the preferred position (mutual cap at the greater of 12 months' fees and USD 1,000,000) and the fallback (mutual cap of 12 months' fees) on a material term. The redline inserts the mutual cap into the existing sentence, keeps the existing Section 13/14 carve-outs and adds indemnification, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and IP infringement as uncapped Excluded Claims, and confirms our fee payment obligations are not "damages" for cap purposes. Note that Section 13, despite its caption, contains no actual indemnity; that gap is for the indemnity rule rather than this one.

proposal.summary: Add a mutual liability cap (greater of 12 months' fees or USD 1,000,000) with uncapped Excluded Claims and fees excluded from the cap
proposal.comment: [Playbook] Section 15 excludes indirect damages but contains no cap at all, so our own exposure for direct damages is unlimited; we have added the mutual cap our playbook requires (greater of 12 months' fees or USD 1,000,000). Indemnification, confidentiality (Section 14), IP (Section 13), gross negligence, wilful misconduct and fraud sit outside the cap, and fees properly due are not treated as damages.

ops.oldText: The limitation of liability in this Section 15 shall not apply to breaches of Sections 13 and 14.
ops.newText: Except for Excluded Claims, each party's total aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall not exceed the greater of (a) the fees paid or payable by Sparkling under this Agreement in the twelve (12) months immediately preceding the event giving rise to the claim and (b) USD 1,000,000. "Excluded Claims" means a party's breach of Section 13 or Section 14, its indemnification obligations, its gross negligence, wilful misconduct or fraud, and its infringement of the other party's intellectual property rights. The limitations and exclusions of liability in this Section 15 shall not apply to Excluded Claims, and Sparkling's obligation to pay fees properly due under this Agreement shall not be treated as damages for the purposes of this Section 15.
